claim: Quantpedia's 'Momentum Factor and Style Rotation Effect' strategy (source paper Tibbs, Eakins, DeShurko): rank six Russell equity style ETFs (small/mid/large-cap value and growth) by 12-month price momentum monthly, go long the winner and short the loser, holding one month. Reported backtest 1972-2005: annualized return 9.25%, Sharpe 0.33, volatility ~16.0%, max drawdown -52.5%. The page discloses no update or decay statement past 2005 and no long-only or recent-window figure.
quote: All performance metrics come from the original 2005 research paper covering historical data through 2005.
limitations: Practitioner summary page, not the original paper text; sample ends 2005 (20+ years old, pre-dates the modern MTUM/QUAL/USMV/VLUE/SIZE single-factor ETFs, all inception 2011-2013); long-short construction and a long-short Sharpe of only 0.33 -- weak by itself. Used only for the cross-sectional-momentum-across-style-ETFs mechanism, not for its literal 1972-2005 return number, which is why K1/K2 are tested fresh in this batch rather than assumed.
independent_replication: No independent third-party live/forward replication of a long-only rotation across the modern liquid single-factor ETF set was found in this or the prior gap-search round (2 targeted web searches, 2026-09-28).
impact_on_spec: Grounds the FACTOR menu (MTUM, QUAL, USMV, VLUE, SIZE) and the mechanism reused (cross-sectional lookback-momentum rotation); this batch tests the already-validated S1-S3 rotation_cell mechanism on this menu against K1/K2, not Quantpedia's own 1972-2005 long-short number.
